candidate_findings.title: Visible-slice loading has no stale-result rejection contract
candidate_findings.claim: Rapid scrolling, retry, thread switching, or overlapping loads can return slices out of order, but the core says only to re-render when a loader returns and does not bind responses to a thread, range, or generation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A stale response can replace the current skeleton window with the wrong range or potentially wrong-thread content, producing misleading GUI truth and privacy risk.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define request identity containing thread ID, projection revision, range, and generation; cancellation; last-valid-result rules; stale-response disposal; idempotent retry; and a deterministic race test.

evidence_refs.excerpt: model providing only the visible slice

candidate_findings.title: Height and search caches omit content and layout revisions
candidate_findings.claim: Match ranges and measured heights are keyed by stable message identity and query, while the same message can stream, expand, collapse, or otherwise change size and text.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Stale byte or character ranges can highlight the wrong text, and stale heights can cause scrollbar drift, jumps, or incorrect target placement.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify offset encoding and cache keys including content revision and relevant layout dimensions; invalidate on stream mutation, rewind, edit, expansion, width, font, scale, and theme changes.

evidence_refs.excerpt: append or update in place the current message node

candidate_findings.title: Message deep links lack an authorization and scoping envelope
candidate_findings.claim: A shared link or URL can resolve a message ID directly through storage, but no thread, project, workspace, account, or permission binding is specified.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Guessable, stale, or cross-scope IDs could reveal message existence or load content outside the user's current authority boundary.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a scoped deep-link grammar, authorization before lookup and display, non-enumeration behavior, revoked/deleted handling, safe error equivalence, and tests for cross-thread and cross-project targets.

evidence_refs.excerpt: URL/deep link to message

candidate_findings.title: Extreme-thread performance has no deterministic pass oracle
candidate_findings.claim: The design claims bounded smooth behavior and no display limit, but pagination remains optional and no latency, frame-time, blank-frame, memory, or test-corpus threshold establishes when virtualization alone is insufficient.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementations can satisfy the structural wording while still visibly stuttering, exhausting memory, or failing on the stated 10k-message case.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Set representative corpora and hardware tiers, p95 and worst-case scroll and update budgets, maximum live nodes and memory, first-slice latency, blank-frame allowance, and a mandatory fallback threshold for paging.

evidence_refs.excerpt: This is an enhancement if virtualization alone is insufficient for extreme thread lengths.
threads with 10k+ messages may need pagination or load-older in addition to virtualization.

candidate_findings.title: Streaming throttle and memory-cap boundaries are underspecified
candidate_findings.claim: The core permits layout at one or two frames per second and caps hot memory at 200 messages or 8 MB, but does not define final flush, cancellation flush, byte accounting, eviction order, or how an active or visible item larger than the cap is pinned.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The final streamed text can remain visually stale, while eviction can remove required visible or active state or repeatedly page-thrash a large message.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define coalescer flush events and maximum display lag; counted byte representation; pinning of visible, active, and unsaved items; oversized-single-item behavior; eviction order; and pressure telemetry.

evidence_refs.excerpt: coalesce into 1-2 frames per second for layout
In-memory cap: last **200 messages** or **8 MB** (whichever limit is reached first).

candidate_findings.title: Superseded UI keys and retired pass selectors lack migration rules
candidate_findings.claim: The core retires pop-out command IDs and persistence keys and separately retires three provider-model selectors, but gives no versioned mapping, precedence, cleanup, rollback, or user-notification behavior for existing installations.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Upgrades can retain conflicting settings, lose user choices, resurrect obsolete controls, or yield different behavior depending on upgrade history.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Provide old-to-new key maps, merge precedence, one-time idempotent migration markers, legacy-read duration, deletion policy, downgrade behavior, and fixture-based upgrade tests.

candidate_findings.title: Dynamic registry fallback contradicts the settings-only determinism invariant

candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Two machines or two times with identical settings can resolve different providers or models, undermining reproducibility and cycle-report interpretation.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Include a versioned registry snapshot in resolution inputs, define a total stable ordering and tie-breaker, clarify that determinism covers the full snapshot rather than settings alone, and test reordered discovery results.

candidate_findings.title: Invalid saved pairs make fallback recursive and warning copy potentially false
candidate_findings.claim: Priority one unconditionally uses a stored pair, while unavailable-provider acceptance says to fall back through the same chain; the chain does not say to exclude the invalid explicit value, and the warning promises an Auditor Model default even when later fallbacks could select chat or first eligible values.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Resolution can loop, retain an invalid pair, choose a provider/model mismatch, or tell the user a different fallback than the one actually executed. Saved-model unavailability is not covered at all.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define validation before priority evaluation, partial-pair behavior, unavailable or ineligible model handling, exclusion of failed candidates, whether invalid values are cleared or retained, exact requested/effective warning data, and no-provider terminal behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Provider/model save and sweep-start snapshot are not atomic
candidate_findings.claim: Provider and model are separate keys, while a sweep must capture the pair active at start; no transaction, revision, compare-and-swap, or concurrent-save rule prevents a mixed pair.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A sweep starting during a settings write can run with a provider from one selection and a model from another, then emit a report that appears valid.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Store the pair atomically with a settings revision; validate pair compatibility before commit; snapshot one resolved record at sweep admission; define concurrent save versus start ordering; and test crash and interleaving cases.

candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementers and serializers cannot tell whether these are forbidden input aliases, accepted compatibility fields, or required output fields, inviting schema divergence and duplicate sources of truth.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Remove deprecated names from the normative list or label each as input-only migration alias with normalization phase, rejection/output rules, telemetry, and retirement date; publish one canonical output schema.

candidate_findings.title: Natural-language Persona matching lacks deterministic intent and confidence rules
candidate_findings.claim: The core uses an undefined reliable-match threshold and discretionary clarification, without distinguishing actual control intent from quoted text, code, examples, negation, or discussion of a Persona command.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Identical input can switch Persona in one implementation and remain ordinary chat in another, and content containing command-like text can trigger an unintended runtime change.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define parsing boundaries, normalization, locale and case rules, alias precedence, confidence thresholds, tie handling, negation and quotation behavior, and table-driven positive and negative test fixtures.

candidate_findings.title: Natural-language subagent invocation lacks an authority and recovery contract
candidate_findings.claim: The phrase surrounding task permits delegation is the only gate before creating or routing a child run; no authority owner, permission check, resource limit, idempotency key, denial state, or child-creation failure behavior is defined here.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A conversational phrase can trigger compute or tool activity without a deterministic authorization decision, or duplicate child runs during retry.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Name the delegation-policy owner and decision inputs; require project, tool, permission, and budget checks; define confirmation thresholds, idempotent creation, cancellation, denial copy, failure recovery, and audit events.

evidence_refs.excerpt: create or route a child run when the surrounding task permits delegation

candidate_findings.title: Runtime remap disclosure has no mandatory presentation oracle

candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A remapped run can meet some listed UI text while still hiding the requested choice, effective surface, or reason from keyboard, touch, collapsed, or post-run views.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define the exact remap states requiring disclosure, mandatory fields, persistent placement available without hover, timing, dismissal, accessibility-neutral interaction, and screenshot or state assertions for denial and fallback.

candidate_findings.title: Opaque-origin postMessage bridge lacks caller authentication and capability controls
candidate_findings.claim: Agent-generated script is intentionally executable and postMessage is the sole bridge, but the core does not require event-source binding, per-frame capability tokens, message schema validation, payload limits, sequence checks, or rate limits.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A forged, stale, confused-deputy, or compromised visual frame could invoke host capabilities or flood the host, and opaque origins prevent relying on ordinary origin equality alone.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a versioned message envelope, exact event.source validation, per-instance nonce or MessagePort handshake, capability list, schema and size validation, replay protection, rate limits, revocation on unmount or navigation, and security tests.

candidate_findings.title: sendPrompt is routed through mutable global UI context
candidate_findings.claim: A visual card queues into the active thread composer and changes meaning based on whether a questionnaire is active, but no source-thread binding, question ID, state snapshot point, navigation cancellation, acknowledgement, or duplicate suppression is specified.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Switching thread or questionnaire state while a bridge message is in flight can send text to the wrong conversation or record it as the wrong answer.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Bind every bridge instance to immutable thread, message, visual, questionnaire, and question revisions; define dispatch-time versus receive-time state; reject stale contexts; return an acknowledged result; and test navigation and questionnaire races.

candidate_findings.title: Link and clipboard bridge calls lack scheme, gesture, and permission policy
candidate_findings.claim: The bridge only distinguishes blank versus self navigation and names a browser route; it does not close URL schemes, canonicalize URLs, require user gestures or confirmation, control referrers, or define clipboard denial and failure behavior.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Generated code could open unsafe local or custom schemes, leak data in URLs, create unsolicited tabs, or overwrite clipboard contents without clear user intent.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Allowlist schemes and destinations, reject credentials and unsafe encodings, define detached-preview versus external-browser policy, require trusted user activation where applicable, add confirmation and referrer rules, and return explicit success or denial results.

candidate_findings.title: Network denial and script containment have no enforcement or resource contract
candidate_findings.claim: The core denies arbitrary external network loads and permits bundled third-party scripts, but sandbox allow-scripts does not itself define network blocking, CPU or memory budgets, watchdog behavior, crash recovery, or integrity verification failure handling.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A visual can still attempt network exfiltration or monopolize rendering resources, and a bad or tampered library can hang or crash the surface without a deterministic fallback.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify iframe CSP and URL interception covering connect, image, media, font, worker, navigation, and websocket channels; integrity verification timing; CPU, memory, timer, worker, and resize budgets; watchdog termination; crash card; retry policy; and telemetry.

candidate_findings.title: Sanitizer profile is not an exact closed contract
candidate_findings.claim: The non-iframe sanitizer delegates to a moving library default and unnamed approved URL-bearing attributes, without pinning a version or defining URI schemes, CSS handling, SVG and MathML policy, canonicalization, malformed markup behavior, or native implementation parity.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Different versions or render paths can accept different active content, and URL or SVG edge cases can bypass an apparently safe tag list.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Pin sanitizer version and configuration; enumerate tags, attributes, protocols, CSS and SVG rules; define preprocessing and postprocessing; deny unknowns by default; publish adversarial fixtures; and require parity across every renderer.

evidence_refs.excerpt: The baseline sanitizer is the standard HTML5 safe subset per DOMPurify `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TAGS` plus approved URL-bearing attributes only

candidate_findings.title: Arbitrary-HTML execution wording conflicts with the HTML/JS visual module
candidate_findings.claim: The section defines a path that executes agent-generated HTML, JavaScript, and CSS under sandbox controls, while its unqualified Rules list says arbitrary HTML must not execute.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An implementer cannot tell whether the prohibition applies only to non-iframe Markdown, to unapproved visual fragments, or to the visual module itself.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define separate normative rules for non-iframe sanitization and iframe execution; define what arbitrary means, the approval and packaging boundary, and explicit positive and negative execution tests.

candidate_findings.title: Mode records leave five required fields without closure
candidate_findings.claim: Plan thoroughness, selection source, selection reason, and override scope are mandatory requested/effective record fields, but this addendum supplies no types, enums, nullability, defaults, precedence, persistence, or validation oracle for them.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Producers and consumers can serialize incompatible values and disagree on when an override ends or why requested and effective modes differ.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Close thoroughness, source, and scope enums; define reason schema, nullability, defaults, normalization, precedence, lifecycle, persistence, compatibility aliases, and round-trip fixtures for every overlay and runtime combination.
